theory.intro: A growing pattern can be recorded in a table of values, linking the step number to the number of items used.
facts: Each row of the pattern gives a pair: the **step number** and the **count**.
If each step adds the same amount, the counts are **multiples**.
A table makes the connection between the two quantities easy to see.
steps: Count the items in the first few steps of the pattern.
Record each step number and its count as a column in the table.
Continue the pattern to fill in further values.

foundation.question_text:
A pattern has $1$, $2$, then $3$ separate triangles.
Each triangle has $3$ counters.
Complete the table for stages $1$ to $3$.

At each stage, a pattern has that many rows of $4$ beads.
Record the bead counts for stages $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$.

A tile pattern shows $5$ tiles in each group and one new group at every stage.
Fill the counts for stages $1$ to $3$.

Each stage has its stage number of separate hexagons, with $6$ marked corners on each.
Build a table for stages $1$ to $4$.

A pattern uses $7$ dots in each column and adds one column per stage.
What row of dot counts belongs under stages $1$, $2$ and $3$?

A design has $8$ small squares in each strip and one strip for each stage.
Record the totals through stage $4$.

development.question_text:
A pattern has $9$ pegs in each ring and one ring per stage.
Complete $\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Stage}&2&3&4&5\\\hline\text{Pegs}&18&\square&36&\square\end{array}$.

Each panel contains $12$ tiles.
Make a table of the number of tiles in $1$, $3$, $5$ and $7$ panels.

A dot design contains $11$ dots per spoke.
Fill the missing stage number: $\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Stage}&2&\square&6\\\hline\text{Dots}&22&44&66\end{array}$.

A pattern uses $14$ counters per frame.
Complete the table at stages $3$, $6$ and $9$.

A mosaic has $15$ tiles in each repeated block.
Its table shows $30$, $60$ and $90$ tiles.
Record the matching stage numbers.

Each shape in a pattern has $13$ marked points.
Extend the table from stage $4$ to stages $5$ and $6$: $\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Stage}&4&5&6\\\hline\text{Points}&52&\square&\square\end{array}$.

mastery.question_text:
A stage-$n$ display consists of $n$ separate stars, each with $16$ lights.
Build a table for stages $2$, $5$, $8$ and $10$.

A table for a pattern with $18$ counters per group contains an error: $\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Stage}&1&2&3&4\\\hline\text{Counters}&18&36&56&72\end{array}$.
Correct it.

A bead pattern uses $24$ beads per section.
The table includes $72$ and $168$ beads.
Find their stage numbers and show them as columns.
